http.protocolVersionPlacement: The v1 route prefix and negotiated vendor media type select protocol v1 for bodyless GET requests. Requests with bodies require protocolVersion. Every application success or error response body requires protocolVersion.
http.correlationRequestHeader: X-Correlation-Id optional bounded caller value; gateway may replace invalid values
http.correlationResponseHeader: X-Correlation-Id required and equal to error envelope correlationId when an envelope exists
http.retryAfter: HTTP Retry-After is required for rate_limit and may accompany dependency; envelope retryAfterMilliseconds is the precise client delay and must agree after rounding Retry-After seconds upward
http.preEnvelopeFailures: TLS, proxy, gateway, body-size, media-negotiation and authentication rejection may lack an application envelope; clients map the HTTP/network condition to a local transport outcome and never treat it as a terminal command receipt

compatibility.unknownOptionalResponseFields: rejected_at_protocol_v1_schema; a later negotiated compatible minor may declare bounded ignorable fields

changeSemantics.upsert: replace the typed entity projection at its revision
changeSemantics.tombstone: the canonical entity was authoritatively deleted; remove canonical entity and view membership
changeSemantics.view_remove: the entity still may exist canonically but is no longer visible in this authorized view; remove view membership and do not delete a shared canonical cache entry solely for this change
changeSemantics.invalidation: discard the named cached projection and refetch through its authorized query/read operation; it is not evidence of canonical deletion

limits.decodedBudgetAccounting: Every value and map key costs one node and 32 units; add 8 units per array slot or 16 per map pair, 2 units per UTF-16 code unit for text (keys included), and binary byte length. Charge declared lengths before allocation; include all nested values and all envelope fields. Units are a deterministic logical allocation cap, not measured heap bytes. Reject if either budget is exceeded; also enforce each local bound.
limits.compression: Content-Encoding absent or identity only; reject compressed request bodies with 415 before decompression; response Content-Encoding identity or absent. Do not advertise Accept-Encoding compression; gateways must not transparently decompress requests.
limits.unicode: Strict UTF-8 scalar values only; reject malformed UTF-8/unpaired surrogates and duplicate keys before lossy materialization; no Unicode normalization. Schema maxLength counts Unicode scalars; also enforce global stringBytes.
limits.retainedCopies: Charge every concurrently retained decoded copy using the same logical allocation formula; no uncharged copy.

normalization.objects: keys sorted by unsigned lexicographic comparison of their UTF-8 byte sequences
normalization.uuid: Validate canonical lowercase diagnostic UUID or decode exactly 16 RFC-order bytes, then encode canonical lowercase UUID text with string tag; never use Guid.ToByteArray native layout.
normalization.int64: Schema-declared signed64 diagnostic decimal strings or exact MessagePack integers normalize to a checked signed integer then integer tag. Compact safe integers have the same tag; unsafe rounded numbers are rejected before conversion.
normalization.timestamp: base10 integer encoded with integer tag
normalization.strings: Unicode scalar sequence encoded as UTF-8 with no implicit normalization
normalization.null: null tag only where schema allows
normalization.numbers: Schema integer fields normalize exact integer tokens, never floating point tokens, fractions, negative zero or diagnostic exponent notation. JSON integer lexical validation precedes object materialization.
normalization.extensions: numeric tokens rejected recursively in core v1; values contain only null, boolean, string, arrays and objects

fingerprint.framing: ASCII gsc1 followed by exactly one value. value := n | f | t | i<minimal-decimal>; | s<unsigned-byte-count>:<UTF-8-bytes> | a<unsigned-count>:[<value><value>...] | o<unsigned-count>:{<key-string>,<value><key-string>,<value>...}. The literal delimiters are i, semicolon, s, colon, a, brackets, o, braces, and one comma between each object key and value; there is no comma between pairs or array items and no whitespace. An object key is a string frame. Counts and lengths are unsigned minimal decimal. Object pairs use the declared UTF-8 key ordering.
fingerprint.note: C03 remains a G1 review choice: approve this tagged grammar or replace it with another fully specified mechanism. The paired vectors cover this proposal; it is not yet a frozen compatibility promise.

conflictCodes.operation_identity_conflict: 409: scoped operationId exists with changed immutable tuple or fingerprint
conflictCodes.stream_sequence_conflict: 409: scoped sequence belongs to a different operation
conflictCodes.stream_retired: 409: unseen command on retired stream; exact terminal replay still returns stored result
conflictCodes.receipt_integrity_unavailable: 503: required retained result missing; never found:false below finalizedThrough
